spine: 1. SQLite 的完整性不是它獨力達成的，而是一整疊承諾的連鎖擔保——OS 保證鎖與 fsync，硬碟保證 sync 完成代表落地。
2. 這疊承諾的技術核心是把 fsync/sync 當成 I/O barrier：barrier 前的寫入必須全部在 barrier 後的寫入之前落地，順序而非時間。
3. SQLite 對底層只能 must believe——沒有辦法偵測 OS 或硬體在 sync 上說謊或亂序，這是它的信任邊界，也是所有 corruption 的溫床。
4. corruption 幾乎從不是 SQLite 出錯，而是某一層安靜毀約：刪 hot journal 讓 recovery 瞎、NFS 鎖 bug、close() 掃掉整個 process 的 advisory lock、碟謊報 sync 導致斷電亂序、交易中途備份得半新半舊。
5. 語氣分層透露風險溫度：文件對機制必然用 will/must/do not，對條件湊齊才會的用 can/might/could。
6. 對工程師的可操作結論：db 檔別放 NFS、fork 後在 child 重開連線、備份用 sqlite3_rsync/VACUUM INTO/backup API、別關 PRAGMA synchronous、別在 db 開著時對它玩 rename/unlink/link。

perspective.mechanism: SQLite 的 atomic commit 靠 journal + fsync；fsync 的語意可弱化為一道 I/O barrier（barrier 前寫入全部先於 barrier 後寫入落地即無 corruption）；SQLite 對 OS/硬體的 sync 回報只能 must believe，無法偵測說謊或亂序。corruption 的各種來源都是某一層對這串承諾毀約。
perspective.tradeoff: durability vs 效能：關掉 sync（PRAGMA synchronous=OFF）或用會謊報 sync 的消費級碟能更快，代價是斷電時寫入可能亂序而 corrupt；把 db 放 NFS 換取共享存取，代價是網路鎖 bug 造成併發寫入 corruption。
perspective.reader_use: 台灣工程師的清單：SQLite 檔不要放 NFS/網路檔案系統；開連線後 fork 要在 child 重開、別在 child 呼叫 sqlite3_close；備份改用 sqlite3_rsync/VACUUM INTO/backup API 而非直接 cp；別為了跑分關 PRAGMA synchronous；別在 db 開著時對檔做 unlink/rename，少用 hard/soft link；crash 後別讓清理腳本刪掉 -journal/-wal。

notes.quote: In order to guarantee that database files are always consistent, SQLite will occasionally ask the operating system to flush all pending writes to persistent storage then wait for that flush to complete. This is accomplished using the fsync() system call under unix and FlushFileBuffers() under Windows. We call this flush of pending writes a 'sync'.
notes.interpretation: SQLite 完整性模型的基礎：commit 過程呼叫 fsync()/FlushFileBuffers() 並等待完成。用來介紹 durability model。

notes.quote: the sync operation can be thought of as an I/O barrier. As long as all writes that occur before the sync are completed before any write that happens after the sync, no database corruption will occur.
notes.interpretation: 關鍵抽象：sync 是 I/O barrier；只要 barrier 前寫入全部先於 barrier 後寫入落地，就 no corruption（此處文件用斷定語氣 will occur 的否定）。整篇技術核心。

notes.quote: Note that SQLite must believe whatever the operating system and hardware tell it about the status of sync requests. There is no way for SQLite to detect that either is lying and that writes might be occurring out-of-order.
notes.interpretation: 信任邊界：SQLite must believe，無法偵測 OS/硬體說謊或亂序。closer 與 spine #3 的直接依據。

notes.quote: Disk drives will report that content is safely on persistent media as soon as it reaches the track buffer and before actually being written to oxide.
notes.interpretation: 碟謊報機制：資料一進 track buffer（揮發性快取）就回報已寫入持久媒體，實際尚未寫到碟片（oxide）。用 will，機制斷定。

notes.quote: if a power loss or hard reset does occur, and if that results in content that was written after a sync reaching oxide while content written before the sync is still in a track buffer, then database corruption can occur.
notes.interpretation: 後果：斷電時 sync 後寫入先落地、sync 前寫入還在 track buffer，順序顛倒 → corruption。hedge = can occur（條件湊齊才會）。scrubber widget 的模型依據。

notes.quote: USB flash memory sticks seem to be especially pernicious liars regarding sync requests... Pulling out the memory stick while the LED is still flashing will frequently result in database corruption.
notes.interpretation: 開頭具體場景：隨身碟謊報 sync；燈還在閃就拔會 frequently result in corruption。frequently 是文件少見的強語氣＋情緒（especially pernicious liars）。hook 依據。

notes.quote: the close() system call will cancel all POSIX advisory locks on the same file for all threads and all file descriptors in the process.
notes.interpretation: POSIX close() 陷阱：任一 thread 的 close() 取消整個 process 對該檔的所有 advisory lock（所有 thread、所有 fd）。文件用 will。tab widget S3 依據。

notes.quote: So, for example, suppose a multi-thread process has two or more threads with separate SQLite database connections to the same database file. Then a third thread comes along and wants to read something out of that same database file on its own, without using the SQLite library... the close() system call caused the locks held on the database by all the other threads to be dropped. Those other threads have no way of knowing that their locks have just been trashed... This can lead to two or more threads or processes trying to write to the database at the same time, resulting in database corruption.
notes.interpretation: close() 事故完整劇本：兩 thread 各持鎖 → 第三 thread 無 SQLite 直接讀＋close() → 其他 thread 的鎖被 dropped 且不知情 → 同時寫入 → corruption。結論句 hedge = can lead to。tab widget 四階段全依此。

notes.quote: The SQLite developers are aware of at least one commercial product that was released with exactly this bug... The problem was eventually traced to the fact that the application was linking against two separate copies of SQLite.
notes.interpretation: 真實案例：某商業產品連結兩份獨立 SQLite，各自維護 open-files 清單互不可見，一份 close() 掃掉另一份鎖。用於「這條坑不是理論」段。

notes.quote: Beginning with SQLite version 3.51.0 (2025-11-04), SQLite implements additional defenses to try to avoid problems caused by locks that are broken by close().
notes.interpretation: 緩解：3.51.0（2025-11-04）加了額外防禦 try to avoid close() 破壞鎖的問題。用於補充「後來補的網」。日期與版本號直引。

notes.quote: If the hot journal files are moved, deleted, or renamed after a crash or power failure, then automatic recovery will not work and the database may go corrupt.
notes.interpretation: hot journal 刪除：crash/斷電後移走/刪/改名 journal → automatic recovery will not work（斷定）→ database may go corrupt（may，條件性）。hot-journal SVG widget＋表格第一列依據。

notes.quote: SQLite depends on the underlying filesystem to do locking as the documentation says it will. But some filesystems contain bugs in their locking logic such that the locks do not always behave as advertised. This is especially true of network filesystems and NFS in particular. If SQLite is used on a filesystem where the locking primitives contain bugs, and if two or more threads or processes try to access the same database at the same time, then database corruption might result.
notes.interpretation: NFS 鎖 bug：網路檔案系統尤其 NFS 的鎖實作常有 bug；併發存取 → corruption might result。applicability 第一條＋表格第二列依據。hedge = might result。

notes.quote: Do not open an SQLite database connection, then fork(), then try to use that database connection in the child process. All kinds of locking problems will result and you can easily end up with a corrupt database.
notes.interpretation: fork() 禁令：全篇最硬祈使句 Do not...；child 用繼承的連線 → you can easily end up with a corrupt database。文件另警告連 sqlite3_close() 在 child 都不行（會觸發 cleanup 刪掉 parent 內容）。applicability 第二條。

notes.quote: The backup copy then might contain some old and some new content, and thus be corrupt.
notes.interpretation: 交易中途備份：得到半舊半新的檔。安全做法（文件另列）：sqlite3_rsync、VACUUM INTO、backup API、或無交易時複製。applicability 第三條＋表格第五列。hedge = might。

notes.quote: By setting PRAGMA synchronous=OFF, all sync operations are omitted. This makes SQLite seem to run faster, but it also allows the operating system to freely reorder writes, which could result in database corruption if a power failure or hard reset occurs prior to all content reaching persistent storage.
notes.interpretation: PRAGMA synchronous=OFF：省掉所有 sync，seem to run faster，但 OS 可自由重排寫入，斷電 could result in corruption。用於 scrubber 段末「親手把說謊的碟模擬出來」與 applicability。hedge = could。

notes.quote: Since rollback journals and WAL files are based on the name of the database file, the two different database files will share the same rollback journal or WAL file. A rollback or recovery for one of the databases might use content from the other database, resulting in corruption.
notes.interpretation: unlink/rename 開著的檔：journal/WAL 依 db 檔名命名；兩個不同 db 共用同一 journal → recovery might use content from the other → corruption。命名假設段依據（POSIX only）。hedge = might。

notes.quote: If a single database file has multiple links (either hard or soft links) then that is just another way of saying that the file has multiple names. If two or more processes open the database using different names, then they will use different rollback journals and WAL files. That means that if one process crashes, the other process will be unable to recover the transaction in progress because it will be looking in the wrong place for the appropriate journal.
notes.interpretation: multiple links：hard/soft link = 多個檔名；不同 process 用不同名開 → 不同 journal 路徑；crash 後另一 process recovery 找錯地方。命名假設段第二顆地雷依據。

notes.quote: a file descriptor was open on a file, then that file descriptor was closed and reopened on an SQLite database. Later, some other thread continued to write into the old file descriptor, not realizing that the original file had been closed already. But because the file descriptor had been reopened by SQLite, the information that was intended to go into the original file ended up overwriting parts of the SQLite database, leading to corruption of the database.
notes.interpretation: fd 重用陷阱：舊 fd 被關後由 SQLite 重開成 db，另一 thread 仍寫舊 fd 號碼，內容覆蓋到 db 中間 → corruption。真實案例：2013-08-30 Fossil 官方 repo 中招——stderr(fd 2) 被誤關（原文 by stunnel, we suspect），被 SQLite 重開為 db，assert() 訊息寫進 db；Fossil 是受害者，不是關 fd 的行為者。應用層毀約段依據。

notes.quote: SQLite version 3.8.1 (2013-10-17) and later refuse to use low-numbered file descriptors for database files.
notes.interpretation: fd 重用的緩解：3.8.1（2013-10-17）起拒絕用低號 fd 開資料庫。日期與版本號直引。

notes.quote: It is important that all connections to the same database file use the same locking protocol. If one application is using POSIX advisory locks and another application is using dot-file locking, then the two applications will not see each other's locks and will not be able to coordinate database access, possibly leading to database corruption.
notes.interpretation: 鎖協定不一致：同一 db 全體連線須用同一鎖協定；POSIX advisory lock vs dot-file locking 互不可見 → 無法協調 → possibly leading to corruption。通常因手動換 sqlite3_vfs 只換一半。applicability「同一種語言」段依據。hedge = possibly。
